clue.text: A city to impress sailors

explanation.surface: A note that a Chinese port is the place to win over seafarers.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb comes from the port: men were once forced onto ships bound for the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Shanghai is China's great port, and to shanghai someone was to drug or trick a man into serving as crew on a ship.

clue.text: Dancer to see in uniform

indicators.note: the word for see goes in the word for uniform

parts.note: uniform means the same throughout
lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Go and watch a dancer in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Salome danced before Herod in the Bible story, earning the head of John the Baptist.

clue.text: Shy relative

parts.note: read 'shy' as a throwing game at a fair rather than timid; the game bears a relative's name

explanation.surface: A timid family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Aunt Sally is a British pub and fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy, hence also a target for abuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The throwing game is a kind of coconut shy named after an aunt.

clue.text: Cold as some eels are said to be

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: jellied eels are a traditional London dish

explanation.surface: Chilly, as eels are described.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels, eels set in their own jelly, are a traditional cheap London dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelid means icy or very cold.

clue.text: Maintained member took part in crooked deal

indicators.note: the limb took a part in, went inside, the bent deal
crooked means bent or twisted out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A claim that someone joined in a dishonest bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' rearranges the fodder into ALED; 'took part in' is the container signal, as the limb enters the bent bargain. 'Maintained' means claimed, not kept up.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or maintain that something is so.

clue.text: Burning a mark on a horse

parts.note: a blaze is a white stripe down the face of a horse

explanation.surface: A branding iron burns a sign into a horse's hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on fire is aflame, alight, burning.

clue.text: An encounter with the unseen?

parts.note: not a ghostly meeting but a romantic meeting with a person one has never seen

explanation.definitionFit: A blind date is a social meeting between two people who have not met before.

clue.text: A light abreast of the vessel

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A lamp shines alongside the ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam means at right angles to a ship's keel, level with its side.

clue.text: What peace-makers try to do is put at risk

explanation.surface: Mediators' efforts are threatened.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is to finish rage, as peace-makers wish; as one it means to imperil.

clue.text: Fast-growing spring flower?

parts.note: read 'Fast' as the Christian fast before Easter: a flower that blooms during that season of fasting, the daffodil

explanation.surface: A quick-sprouting bloom of springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild daffodil is named after the Lenten season in which it flowers.

clue.text: Being aroused before daybreak to supply engine part

indicators.note: being stirred up, the letters of the word are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the break, or opening, of 'day' is its first letter, D

explanation.surface: A creature woken before dawn to help supply a part for an engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aroused' rearranges BEING into BIGEN; 'daybreak' gives D, its start.
explanation.definitionFit: The big end is the larger end of a connecting rod, fixed to the crankshaft of an engine.

clue.text: Strikers attempt to get a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a stab is an attempt or try

explanation.surface: Workers on strike try to win a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get a rise' reads STAB upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats are what batters strike the ball with.

clue.text: Thought a great many were employed

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a great many
things that were employed were used

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that lots of people had jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder, so mused means pondered, reflected.

clue.text: Soldiers possibly armed with guns

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may form another arrangement than the one shown

explanation.surface: Troops who may well be carrying firearms.
explanation.definitionFit: Guardsmen are soldiers of a regiment of Guards.

clue.text: Old man may be a tough nut to crack

indicators.note: cracking something breaks it up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An elderly man can be a difficult person to win over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tough nut to crack' is an idiom for a difficult person; here 'to crack' breaks up OLD MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is a hard-shelled nut.

clue.text: Reserved, but singularly partisan

explanation.surface: Quiet, yet oddly biased.
explanation.definitionFit: Set aside is reserved; taking a single camp is partisan.

clue.text: A bit that's appropriate

explanation.surface: A small piece that is fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A snaffle is a simple jointed bit for a horse's mouth, and to snaffle is to seize or take for oneself, as to appropriate is.

clue.text: Like ports equipped for defence

explanation.surface: Harbours are armed against attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a wine strengthened with brandy, and a town with walls and guns is strengthened against attack.

clue.text: Calculating a pudding mixture

indicators.note: a pudding mixture is stirred together, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Measuring out ingredients for a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up is totting up figures, working out a sum.

clue.text: Large basin that usually doesn't hold water

definitions.text: Large basin that usually doesn't hold water

parts.words: Large basin that usually doesn't hold water
parts.note: a basin for ships that is pumped empty so a hull can be worked on: a basin kept without water

explanation.surface: A big washbowl that leaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A dry dock is a dock that is drained so a ship's hull can be repaired.

clue.text: Famous Shakespearean actor sounds enthusiastic

indicators.note: sounds says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: keen means enthusiastic

explanation.surface: A great Shakespearean performer is eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmund Kean was a celebrated English tragic actor in Shakespeare roles.

clue.text: Applause is so long

explanation.surface: Clapping goes on for a good while.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers are shouts of acclaim, and 'cheers' is also an informal British goodbye, like 'so long'.

clue.text: Mouse-catcher not yet used in the plant

parts.note: a cat catches mice
mint, as in mint condition, means new and unused

explanation.surface: A cat that is unused in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint is a herb also called catnip, which cats love.

clue.text: A race tip? Listen!

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
a tip is an end

explanation.surface: A betting tip offered with a call to pay heed.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend is to pay attention, to listen closely.

clue.text: Formerly patients treated outside hospital

indicators.note: the rearranged patients stand outside, around, the hospital letter
treated, as in worked on, says the letters are processed into a new order

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: In earlier days, people were cared for as outpatients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges PATIENTS into INTEPAST, and 'outside' puts that around H.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly means at an earlier time, in days gone by.

clue.text: Persuade casual worker to be on time

indicators.note: in a down clue being on another piece means sitting above it

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker

explanation.surface: Coaxing a part-time employee to be punctual.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt is to entice or coax someone.

clue.text: It may be smoked and eaten

definitions.text: It may be smoked and eaten

parts.words: It may be smoked and eaten
parts.note: two things share a name: a cannabis cigarette is smoked, a cut of meat (perhaps smoked) is eaten

explanation.definitionFit: A joint is both a roll-up of cannabis and a large cut of roast meat.

clue.text: Wild jaunt for council workers

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A rowdy outing for municipal employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a ruling committee or council, a body of people working together to govern.

clue.text: Good opening with scope for clever move on board

indicators.note: the opening of the word Good is its first letter

parts.note: an ambit is the scope or extent of something

explanation.surface: A strong chess start that leaves room for a smart play.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambit is a chess opening in which a piece is sacrificed for advantage, a clever play on the board.

clue.text: Major report produced by a VIP

parts.note: major means big
a report is a loud bang, a noise

explanation.surface: An important announcement from a dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig or important person is informally called a big noise.

clue.text: Letter bound to have shown sympathy

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A correspondence obliged to express compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: To pity is to feel sorrow for another, so having pitied is having shown sympathy.

clue.text: Whales have been known to be beached and abandoned

definitions.text: Whales have been known to be beached

explanation.surface: Whales sometimes end up washed ashore and left.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranded describes whales run aground on a beach, and also anyone left helpless and deserted.
